title: Encode and Decode Strings
prompt:
Design an algorithm to **encode** a list of strings into one string, and **decode** it back to the original list. The strings can contain ANY characters (commas, `#`, spaces, empty strings) — so a naive `join(",")` won't work.

To make this testable here, implement two private helpers `encode(List<String>)` and `decode(String)`, and the graded method returns `decode(encode(strs))` — it must reproduce the input exactly.

tests.note: delimiter and digits inside the data

hints: Any separator character you choose could also appear inside one of the strings. How could the decoder know where a string ends without searching for a special character?
Write each string's length before it, followed by a separator: `<length>#<string>`. The decoder reads the number, then takes exactly that many characters — whatever they are.
Decode with an index `i`: scan `j` from i to the `#`, parse `s.substring(i, j)` as the length, take `s.substring(j + 1, j + 1 + len)`, then set `i = j + 1 + len`.

solution.explanation: Insight: length-prefix framing is delimiter-proof. The decoder only looks for `#` inside the length prefix (which is all digits), then reads a fixed count of characters, so payloads may contain `#`, digits, commas, or be empty. Each chunk is consumed exactly, leaving `i` at the start of the next prefix. O(total characters) time and space.
